newsitem.title: UK: Moody's says may downgrade Turkey ratings.
newsitem.headline: Moody's says may downgrade Turkey ratings.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service said on Thursday it placed under review for possible downgrade the Ba3 long-term foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bonds of the Republic of Turkey.
Moody's said it also placed under review for possible downgrade Turkey's B1 foreign currency sovereign ceiling for bank deposits.

"Moody's said that its action was related to the continuing deterioration of Turkey's fiscal situation and the apparent inability of the authorities to take measures that would address the structural causes of the budget deficit," Moody's said in a statement.
The public sector borrowing requirement was estimated to have exceeded 10 percent of GDP in 1996.
"It appears that excessive fiscal stimulus has contributed to an overheating of the economy which, in turn, has resulted in a substantial widening of the current account deficit," Moody's said.

Moody's noted that in the absence of corrective measures, there was a risk that higher inflation could potentially destabilise financial markets and complicate the government's debt servicing position.
"While the government's renewed commitment to privatisation was encouraging, official estimates of revenues from the program appeared optimistic," the statment said.
In addition, Moody's pointed out that without complementary fiscal reforms, privatisation alone could not correct Turkey's underlying fiscal imbalance.
Moody's said that its review would focus on fiscal policy, in particular, the government's net borrowing requirement going forward.
Moody's said it would also closely examine the vulnerability of Turkey's external debt servicing capacity to developments in its domestic financial markets.
